proposals.before: For at that time agriculture was vigorously encouraged and wasteland was reclaimed; no land lay fallow, people devoted themselves to primary occupations; military colonies and the salt monopoly were also established to supply border troops, so transport grain did not depend on county officials — hence both court and countryside had enough, and army and people alike were affluent.
proposals.after: For at that time agriculture was vigorously encouraged and wasteland was reclaimed; no land lay fallow, people devoted themselves to primary occupations; military colonies and the salt-exchange system were also established to supply border troops, so transport grain did not depend on county officials — hence both court and countryside had enough, and army and people alike were affluent.
proposals.reason: 中鹽 denotes the kaizhong salt-certificate exchange for frontier supply, not a salt monopoly; the idiomatic rendering already has the correct sense.

proposals.before: The Ming dynasty's methods of managing wealth over one reign — how they first gained and finally lost — are set forth in outline, root and branch, in this treatise.
proposals.after: The Ming dynasty's methods of managing wealth throughout the dynasty — how they first gained and finally lost — are set forth in outline, root and branch, in this treatise.
proposals.reason: 明一代 means the Ming dynasty as a whole (one dynastic generation), not a single reign.

proposals.before: Those who moved abroad for legitimate reasons and registered locally were called attached-registration households (fuji).
proposals.after: Those who for some reason went to sojourn elsewhere were called attached-registration households (fuji).
proposals.reason: 出僑於外 means residing away from one's original locality, not going abroad; the Chinese also does not add a separate 'registered locally' clause beyond naming the category 附籍.

proposals.before: Those who for some reason went to live abroad were called attached registration.
proposals.after: Those who for some reason went to sojourn elsewhere were called attached registration.
proposals.reason: 外 here means outside the home register locality, not a foreign country.

proposals.before: Censor-in-chief Li Bin presented his proposal to the throne.
proposals.after: Censor-in-chief Li Bin presented this proposal to the throne.
proposals.reason: 其說 refers to Zhou Hongmo's On Floating Populations just cited, not a proposal authored by Li Bin; 'his' misassigns authorship.

proposals.before: The Xianzong Emperor ordered Yuan Jie to go out as pacification commissioner; he recruited one hundred and twenty thousand floating households, granted idle land, established Yun Prefecture, and set up Shangjin and other counties to govern them.
proposals.after: The Xianzong Emperor ordered Yuan Jie to go out as pacification commissioner; he recruited one hundred and twenty thousand floating households, granted idle land, established Yunyang Prefecture, and set up Shangjin and other counties to govern them.
proposals.reason: 鄖陽府 is Yunyang Prefecture; literal 'Yun Prefecture' drops 陽 and obscures the place-name.

proposals.before: In 1373 a deputy minister of the Palace Stud said: "Within Ningxia and in Sichuan from the southwest to Chuancheng and northeast to Tatan — eight hundred li apart — the soil is rich; displaced persons should be recruited for garrison farming."
proposals.after: In 1373 Palace Stud Deputy Liang Ye Xiantiemuer said: "Within Ningxia and in Sichuan from the southwest to Chuancheng and northeast to Tatan — eight hundred li apart — the soil is rich; displaced persons should be recruited for garrison farming."
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits the named official 樑埜仙帖木爾 present in the Chinese and literal fields.

proposals.before: Generals including Deng Yu and Tang He established colonies across Shaanxi, Zhangde, Runing, Beiping, and Yongping, while Zhending migrants were resettled at Fengyang.
proposals.after: Generals including Deng Yu and Tang He established colonies across Shaanxi, Zhangde, Runing, Beiping, and Yongping, while people of Shanxi and Zhending were moved to colonize Fengyang.
proposals.reason: Chinese 徙山西真定民 means migrants from Shanxi and Zhending; idiomatic drops Shanxi and reads only Zhending.

proposals.before: At this time Deng Yu, Tang He, and other generals were dispatched to colonize Shaanxi, Zhangde, Runing, Beiping, and Yongping; people of Zhending in Shanxi were moved to colonize at Fengyang.
proposals.after: At this time Deng Yu, Tang He, and other generals were dispatched to colonize Shaanxi, Zhangde, Runing, Beiping, and Yongping; people of Shanxi and Zhending were moved to colonize at Fengyang.
proposals.reason: Literal treats 山西真定 as Zhending in Shanxi; the paired place-names are Shanxi and Zhending, not a Shanxi jurisdiction of Zhending.

proposals.before: Pang Shangpeng directed salt colonies along the north Yangzi, then moved to the nine frontier commands, working with Regional Commander Wang Chonggu to draft detailed colony plans.
proposals.after: Pang Shangpeng directed salt colonies along the north Yangzi, then moved to the nine frontier commands, working with Governor-General Wang Chonggu to draft detailed colony plans.
proposals.reason: Chinese 總督 denotes a governor-general, not a regional commander (總兵); the idiomatic rendering misidentifies Wang Chonggu's office.

proposals.before: Pang Shangpeng oversaw salt colonies on the north bank of the Yangzi, soon transferred to the nine border zones; with regional commander Wang Chonggu he successively laid out colony policy in great detail.
proposals.after: Pang Shangpeng oversaw salt colonies on the north bank of the Yangzi, soon transferred to the nine border zones; with governor-general Wang Chonggu he successively laid out colony policy in great detail.
proposals.reason: Literal likewise mistranslates 總督 as regional commander; the office is governor-general.

proposals.before: Censor Zuo Guangdou ordered River Intendant Lu Guanxiang to expand paddy cultivation; Vice Minister of Rites Dong Yingju continued the effort.
proposals.after: Censor Zuo Guangdou ordered River Intendant Lu Guanxiang to expand paddy cultivation; Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Dong Yingju continued the effort.
proposals.reason: 太常少卿 is Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices (Taichang), not Vice Minister of Rites (禮部侍郎).

proposals.before: Censor Zuo Guangdou ordered river intendant Lu Guanxiang greatly to expand the benefits of paddy fields; Vice Minister of Rites Dong Yingju followed in carrying this out.
proposals.after: Censor Zuo Guangdou ordered river intendant Lu Guanxiang greatly to expand the benefits of paddy fields; Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Dong Yingju followed in carrying this out.
proposals.reason: Literal likewise mistranslates 太常少卿 as Vice Minister of Rites.

proposals.before: When Chenghua took the throne, Cao Xiangji's confiscated property became palace estates — the term imperial estates dates from this.
proposals.after: When Chenghua took the throne, Cao Jixiang's confiscated property became palace estates — the term imperial estates dates from this.
proposals.reason: 曹吉祥 is Cao Jixiang; Xiangji reverses the given-name syllables.

proposals.before: When Xianzong took the throne, confiscated lands of Cao Xiangji became palace estate fields — the name imperial estates began here.
proposals.after: When Xianzong took the throne, confiscated lands of Cao Jixiang became palace estate fields — the name imperial estates began here.
proposals.reason: Same personal-name error as in the idiomatic field: 吉祥 is Jixiang.

proposals.before: Yet on that day presentations did not cease; memorial petitions also grew ever more numerous.
proposals.after: Yet at that time presentations did not cease; memorial petitions also grew ever more numerous.
proposals.reason: 當日 here means at that time in narrative prose, not a single calendar day.

proposals.before: Yet much was pocketed by eunuchs at the temples; accumulated arrears reaching hundreds of thousands became the norm.
proposals.after: Yet much was pocketed by eunuchs; accumulated arrears reaching hundreds of thousands became the norm.
proposals.reason: 宦寺 is a standard metonym for eunuchs, not literal temple locations; 'at the temples' invents a place reading.

proposals.before: In Jiajing 39, Censor Shen Shu recovered more than 16,000 qing of concealed manor land.
proposals.after: In Jiajing 39, Censor Shen Yang recovered more than 16,000 qing of concealed manor land.
proposals.reason: Chinese personal name is 瀋陽 (Shen Yang); English Shen Shu does not match the source characters.

proposals.before: In the thirty-ninth year of Jiajing, Censor Shen Shu was dispatched to clear concealed and falsely registered estate fields of more than sixteen thousand qing.
proposals.after: In the thirty-ninth year of Jiajing, Censor Shen Yang was dispatched to clear concealed and falsely registered estate fields of more than sixteen thousand qing.
proposals.reason: Chinese personal name is 瀋陽 (Shen Yang); English Shen Shu does not match the source characters.

proposals.before: Under Jiajing, Chengtian's six estates and two lakes totaled 8,300-odd qing under eunuch control; school estates annexed another 880 qing, split into twelve manors.
proposals.after: Under Jiajing, Chengtian's six estates and two lakes totaled 8,300-odd qing under eunuch control; guard residences annexed another 880 qing, split into twelve manors.
proposals.reason: 校舍 in this imperial-estate context means residences of imperial guards or retainers, not school estates.

proposals.before: At first, in Shizong's reign, the six estates and two lakes of Chengtian totaled 8,300-odd qing, supervised by eunuch officials; school estates were also permitted to merge and annex, increasing by 880 qing, divided into twelve estates.
proposals.after: At first, in Shizong's reign, the six estates and two lakes of Chengtian totaled 8,300-odd qing, supervised by eunuch officials; residences of imperial guards were also permitted to merge and annex, increasing by 880 qing, divided into twelve estates.
proposals.reason: 校舍 in this imperial-estate context means residences of imperial guards or retainers, not school estates.

decisions.reason: 中鹽 is the frontier-supply salt exchange, not a general salt monopoly.

decisions.reason: 明一代 refers to the whole Ming dynasty in this retrospective statement.

decisions.reason: 出僑於外 means sojourning outside one's home registration area, not traveling abroad, and the proposed wording removes an invented second registration clause.

decisions.reason: The source explicitly names 鄖陽府, Yunyang Prefecture.

Zhending was not being identified as a place in Shanxi; both Shanxi and Zhending supplied settlers.
總督 is Governor-General and must not be confused with the military office 總兵.
The literal field repeats the same confusion of 總督 with Regional Commander.

The literal field contains the same reversed given-name spelling.
當日 refers to the period being discussed, as confirmed by the continuing pattern of presentations and petitions, not one calendar day.

decisions.after: Under Jiajing, Chengtian's six estates and two lakes totaled 8,300-odd qing under eunuch control; imperial guards and hereditary military retainers were also permitted to annex land, adding another 880 qing and creating twelve manors.
decisions.reason: 校舍 abbreviates the personnel categories 校尉 and 舍人 in Ming usage. It refers to imperial guards and hereditary military retainers, not school estates or guard residences.

decisions.after: At first, during Shizong's reign, the six estates and two lakes of Chengtian totaled more than 8,300 qing and were administered by eunuchs; imperial guards and hereditary military retainers were also allowed to annex land, adding 880 qing, and the holdings were divided into twelve estates.
decisions.reason: The literal field should expand 校舍 as the personnel categories 校尉 and 舍人; the proposal's 'residences' still treats 舍 as a building.
